questions.heading: A Budget Matrix Has One Row per Constraint and One Column per Decision
questions.stem: A model decides which of 30 substations to inspect. It has a spending limit for each of 5 months and a crew-hour limit for each of the same 5 months, and nothing else. Written as Ax ≤ b, what shape is A?

options.text: 30 rows by 10 columns, one row per substation and one column per limit
options.says: That is the transpose: rows are constraints and columns are the decisions, here the substations.

options.text: 10 rows by 30 columns, one row per limit and one column per substation
options.says: Right: each of the 10 limits is a row, and each yes/no inspection decision is a column.

options.text: 5 rows by 30 columns, one row per month and one column per substation
options.says: Money and crew-hours in a month are two different rules with different coefficients, so they are two rows.

options.text: 30 rows by 30 columns, one row and one column per substation
options.says: A need not be square: it has as many rows as constraints, whatever the number of variables.

questions.heading: Every Linear Rule Fits Ax ≤ b: Flip ≥ Rows, Split = Rows
questions.stem: A model has five binary variables x1 to x5. A new rule says at least 2 of projects 1, 3 and 4 go ahead. Which row of Ax ≤ b states it?

options.text: Coefficients (1, 0, 1, 1, 0) with right-hand side 2, keeping both sides as written
options.says: As a ≤ row this says at most 2, the opposite rule; an at-least rule must be multiplied by -1 first.

options.text: Coefficients (-1, 0, -1, -1, 0) with right-hand side 2, negating only the left side
options.says: Multiplying by -1 applies to both sides; this row says the sum is at least -2, which every plan meets.

options.text: Coefficients (1, 0, 1, 1, 0) with right-hand side -2, negating only the right side
options.says: This says the sum is at most -2, which no 0/1 plan can meet; the coefficients must change sign too.

options.text: Coefficients (-1, 0, -1, -1, 0) with right-hand side -2, negating both sides
options.says: Right: x1 + x3 + x4 ≥ 2 times -1 is -x1 - x3 - x4 ≤ -2.

questions.heading: Ax ≤ b Checks Every Row at Once
questions.stem: For one plan, a model's row activities are Ax = (120, 300, 75) and its limits are b = (150, 300, 60), in whole $k. What does the slack b - Ax say about the three rows?

options.text: Row 1 has 30 to spare, row 2 is tight, and row 3 is broken by 15
options.says: Right: the slack is (30, 0, -15); zero means met exactly and negative means broken.

options.text: Row 1 is broken by 30, row 2 is tight, and row 3 has 15 to spare
options.says: The signs are reversed: positive slack is room to spare, and negative slack is a broken row.

options.text: Row 1 has 30 to spare, row 2 is broken, and row 3 is broken by 15
options.says: A row met with equality holds; ≤ includes equal, so row 2 is tight, not broken.

options.text: Row 1 has 30 to spare, row 2 is tight, and row 3 is within its tolerance
options.says: A tolerance forgives rounding a hair off the limit; with whole $k there is no rounding, and 15 is a real overrun.
